name: FreeGenVideo
tagline: Create short videos from text prompts or reference images in a browser
description:
FreeGenVideo is an AI video generator that runs in the browser. Its homepage says it turns a text prompt, or a starting image plus a prompt, into a video. The same page says you can use it with no sign-up, no login, and no app to install, and that you should check the allowance shown in the generator before you start. Guest use is described as available when that free allowance is offered.

The free allowance on the homepage is one video per day. It resets at 00:00 UTC. Text to video starts from a written prompt. Image to video starts from an uploaded image plus a prompt. The uploader accepts PNG, JPG, and WebP files, up to 5 MB each. The first image is the start frame. A second image can be an end frame, and the control on the page labels that option 540P and 5 seconds. Other output settings depend on the model selected in the generator. The homepage says the example clips were generated with Seedance 2.0, and that results vary with the prompt, the reference image, and the model.

The steps on the site are to describe who or what is in the shot, what happens, and how the camera moves; add an image if you want image to video; then preview the result and save it. The page names three uses: a social clip or personal project, a story or animation idea, and a product or ad concept. It says to review the video before publishing. The FAQ says a result will not always match the prompt, and that generated videos are private by default. Prompts, starting images, and the request data needed to run the job are sent to the AI provider for the model in use.

The terms of service, last updated 2026-10-22, say the service is operated by FreeGenVideo. They describe credits and subscriptions. Prices, currency, credit quantities, and billing intervals are shown before checkout, and Stripe processes card payments. No dollar price was printed on the homepage, the terms, the privacy policy, or the sitemap checked on November 12, 2026. The privacy policy of the same date says an account can sign in with Google or GitHub. For guest generation, the site stores a keyed hash of a ThumbmarkJS browser fingerprint so it can apply device limits. It says it does not store the underlying fingerprint components.

The homepage says the generator runs in a phone, tablet, or computer browser. No app install is required.
